newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka aims to bypass politics to end war.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka aims to bypass politics to end war.

text.p: Sri Lanka's ruling People's Alliance and the main opposition United National Party (UNP) have agreed to work together to end the country's protracted ethnic war, the government said on Thursday.

Sri Lankan Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar said in a statement on behalf of President Chandrika Kumaratunga and opposition leader Ranil Wickremesinghe that the two parties were aiming at a "common approach" to solve the crisis.

"The president and the leader of the opposition have exchanged letters about a number of arrangements which are intended to develop a common, cross-party approach -- a bipartisan approach -- towards the resolution of the ethnic conflict in our country," Kadirgamar said in his statement.

The two leaders, in similar letters to each other, agreed that the head of the government would seek the opinion of opposition leaders on significant developments relating to the ethnic conflict, regardless of the party in power.

They also agreed that the party in opposition should not undermine any discussions or decisions between the ruling party and any other group, including the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, aimed at ending the conflict.

The LTTE have been fighting for an independent homeland for the country's minority Tamils in the north and east since 1983. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the conflict.
